framing: SAATH delivers culturally-adapted Cognitive Stimulation Therapy (CST) — a named, evidence-based psychosocial intervention. Every activity below is a digital version of a specific session theme from the 14-session CST programme, not an invented game.
principles: Opinions over facts — no one is ever told they are 'wrong'; mistakes get a gentle retry.
Recognition over recall — choices are always shown, never a blank to fill.
Orientation woven in gently — time of day, season and date as conversation.
Multi-sensory — every prompt is spoken aloud as well as shown.
Personalised & culturally relevant — household objects and routines from North-East India, replaced by the family's own photos when available.
Fun and respectful — adult tone, no childish rewards, always-available Pause / Skip / Stop.
evidence: Cochrane systematic review of 15 RCTs (718 participants): consistent significant benefit to cognitive function following treatment, over and above medication effects, sustained at follow-up up to three months. (Aguirre, Woods, Spector & Orrell, Ageing Research Reviews, 2013; Cochrane CD005562)
2024 systematic review & meta-analysis of the original 14-session CST protocol: strong evidence of positive treatment effects for global cognition, language and quality of life.
Official guidelines exist for adapting CST to other cultures (Aguirre, Spector & Orrell) — cultural adaptation for NER is a documented methodology, not improvisation.
2025 systematic review on personalisation: personalised activities are associated with greater engagement and adherence.
NICE NG97 recommends offering group cognitive stimulation to people with mild-to-moderate dementia.
honestLimit: CST has evidence. Our digital, one-to-one delivery of it does not yet — that is what a pilot would test.

mapping.label: Today & Me
mapping.cstTheme: Reality-orientation conversation: part of day, season, weekday and month, drawn live from the device clock.
mapping.note: Every answer is affirmed with the true fact spoken aloud, so the activity orients rather than tests.

mapping.label: Hear & Find
mapping.cstTheme: Hear a spoken word — or a family member's recorded voice — and find the matching picture among distractors.
mapping.note: Visual-only mode shows the word instead, so hearing loss is never penalised.

mapping.label: Sort the Home
mapping.cstTheme: Sort everyday NER household objects into Kitchen, Getting ready and Around the house.
mapping.note: Categories and objects grow with difficulty; shape and label are always shown, never colour alone.

mapping.label: My Next Step
mapping.cstTheme: Put the steps of a familiar daily routine in order.
mapping.note: Uses the family's own approved routine when one exists; otherwise a generic morning, afternoon or evening routine.

mapping.label: Together Moment
mapping.cstTheme: Shared reminiscence around family photos and voices, or open CST discussion prompts.
mapping.note: No score, no streak — a shared conversation. Reminiscence can cause distress (Alzheimer's Society guidance) — exit and content rejection are always available.
